# How to Search Your Notes and Emails with Just Your Voice

You scribbled a quick pasta recipe in your notes app three weeks ago. You tucked the school newsletter with excursion dates into your email folder last month. Now you need that recipe for tonight’s dinner, or that excursion date for tomorrow’s calendar. But scrolling through folders and typing feels like too much effort.

What if you could just say aloud, “Find the pasta recipe I saved,” and have the exact paragraph read back to you in seconds? That’s what the latest AI voice search features let you do: search your own notes, emails, and saved links simply by speaking.

---

## Turn on the listening librarian

First, you need to let the AI know where to look. On most phones and smart speakers this is called “app permissions” or “connected services.”

- **On an iPhone**
  Go to **Settings > Siri & Search > Siri & Dictation > App Library**.
  Turn on access for **Notes, Mail, and Files**.

- **On an Android phone**
  Open the **Google app > Settings > Voice > Voice Match**.
  Make sure “Hey Google” is on and allow access to **Drive, Keep, and Messages**.

- **On a smart speaker (Google Nest, HomePod, etc.)**
  Open the speaker’s app, find **Connected apps**, and add your email account plus any note-taking apps you use.

Once you’ve switched these on, the AI can search across your emails, saved articles, and notes—all from a single voice request.

---

## Speak naturally, get answers fast

You don’t need to learn a special voice or memorise commands. Just talk the way you already do with friends or family.

- “Remind me what the email said about the plumbing repair.”
- “Show me the travel tip I saved from last year.”
- “What was the key point in that article about growing tomatoes?”

The AI will scan your files and read back the exact paragraph. It’s not guessing—it’s pulling from your own words.

**Quick tip:** Start with clear, specific requests. Instead of “Tell me about gardening,” try “What’s the best time to plant tomatoes in Melbourne?” The more precise your question, the better the answer.

---

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Save articles, recipes, or DIY guides in your notes app. Ask aloud while cooking or tidying up, “What’s the first step in making that sourdough bread?” and get the exact line without opening an app.
- **For parents:** Save kids’ school newsletters and activity schedules in your notes. Ask, “When is the next school excursion?” and get the exact date without opening an app.
- **If you’re just getting started:** Pick one topic you care about (cooking, fitness, DIY) and save a few articles or notes. Try asking one question aloud today.

---

## Wrap-up

You don’t need to be tech-savvy to use AI voice search. Start by talking naturally to your phone or smart speaker, teach it where to look, and ask simple questions. Try it today: open your voice assistant, ask one question, and see how it pulls answers from your own notes.
